title: PostgresAI vs New Relic: open source with experts vs queries tied to traces
description: New Relic collects Postgres slow queries, wait events and plans and links them to app traces. PostgresAI is open source and gives AI agents its Issues over MCP.
summary: New Relic is an observability platform. Its PostgreSQL integration with query performance monitoring, generally available since July 2025, collects slow queries, wait events, blocking sessions and execution plan metrics, and Database 360 correlates database behavior with app traces. PostgresAI monitors PostgreSQL only, runs scheduled checkups and turns findings into Issues that you, your AI agent or a PostgresAI expert can act on. Pick New Relic if you already use it and want Postgres queries linked to the traces that ran them. Pick PostgresAI for open-source monitoring you can self-host, Postgres health checks with expert help, or DBLab clones to test a fix.
chooseThem: Database 360 correlates Postgres behavior with the app traces and infrastructure entities around it, and analyzes slow queries with plans, waits and locks.
A perpetual free tier with 100 GB of data ingest a month and one full platform user, so a small setup can start at $0.
Query performance monitoring records execution plan nodes per query, with node type, index used, estimated costs and rows removed by filter, plus per-query CPU and execution time.
Postgres query monitoring includes blocking sessions and wait events per query, with query text normalized and anonymized before it is sent.
The PostgreSQL integration, nri-postgresql, is open source under the MIT license, and an OpenTelemetry-based PostgreSQL integration was added as a public preview in August 2026.

proofs.them: New Relic Ground Truth, its MCP server, needs a paid plan. Its tools run NRQL queries and analyze transactions, logs, traces and metrics; the tool reference lists no database-specific tools.

New Relic's PostgreSQL integration, nri-postgresql, is open source under the MIT license and sends data to the New Relic platform, a paid service with a free tier of 100 GB of ingest a month. The sources we reviewed do not describe a self-hosted backend.

New Relic editions include product support, from a 2-business-day response SLA on Standard to a 1-hour critical response SLA on Enterprise. The sources we reviewed do not describe PostgreSQL expert help.

rows.them: An observability platform. For PostgreSQL, an on-host integration collects metrics and, with query performance monitoring turned on, slow queries, wait events, blocking sessions and execution plans. Database 360 correlates database behavior with app traces and infrastructure.

The infrastructure agent and integration run on a host with network access to the database. The guide covers SSL settings for Amazon RDS and Aurora and Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. The OpenTelemetry integration, added as a public preview in August 2026, documents hosted and Amazon RDS setups.

The New Relic infrastructure agent runs on a host you choose and sends data to New Relic; storage in the EU data center costs an extra $0.05/GB a month. Query text is normalized and anonymized. The sources we reviewed do not describe a self-hosted New Relic backend.
The PostgreSQL integration, nri-postgresql, is open source under the MIT license. New Relic itself is a paid service with a free tier.

Slow queries, individual queries and execution plan metrics from pg_stat_statements. Queries slower than a threshold, 1 ms by default, are sent, with 20 records per metric by default. A dashboard has query analysis, query details and wait time analysis tabs.

Query performance monitoring collects PostgreSQL wait events and blocking sessions, shown in a wait time analysis tab and a blocking details widget. The OpenTelemetry integration, added as a public preview in August 2026, also samples wait events and blocking PIDs; this is off by default.

Not documented in the sources we reviewed. The query performance monitoring page mentions recommendations for query optimization; the sources we reviewed do not describe scheduled health checks for PostgreSQL.

New Relic Ground Truth, a New Relic-hosted MCP server for paid plans, with setup for Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, VS Code and others. Its tools run NRQL queries and analyze transactions and metrics; the tool reference lists no database-specific tools.
Not documented in the sources we reviewed.

Product support by edition: ticketed support with a 2-business-day response SLA on Standard, a 2-hour critical initial response SLA on Pro and 1 hour on Enterprise. The sources we reviewed do not describe PostgreSQL consulting.
Alert workflows notify email, Slack, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams, Opsgenie, Jira, ServiceNow, AWS EventBridge, webhooks and other destinations.
Infrastructure integration data is kept 395 days (13 months) with the original data option and 485 days (16 months) with Data Plus.
New Relic lists SOC 1, SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, FedRAMP, PCI DSS, TISAX and HIPAA enabled capabilities.

faq.q: Does New Relic show PostgreSQL wait events and execution plans?
faq.a: Yes, with query performance monitoring turned on in the PostgreSQL integration. It collects slow queries, wait events, blocking sessions, individual queries and execution plan metrics. New Relic announced this as generally available on July 22, 2025.

faq.q: Does New Relic work with Amazon RDS?
faq.a: Yes. The integration runs on a host with network access to the database, and the guide covers SSL settings for Amazon RDS and Aurora and Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server.

There is a free tier with 100 GB of ingest a month. Paid plans bill full platform users ($10 for the first and $99 for each additional on Standard, $349 a user on Pro with an annual commitment) and data ingest at $0.40/GB beyond 100 GB.

faq.q: Can I use PostgresAI and New Relic together?
faq.a: Yes. DBLab, the PostgresAI cloning product, copies any PostgreSQL source, so a team that monitors with New Relic can test an index or query change on a full-size DBLab clone before production.
